summary: Created so lipsync leaves MPI-4's umbrella and can start. Scope is BENCH AUTHORING ONLY: author and prove the graph on 8188, app integration follows as its own Flow card. Deliberately maturity=planned, not blocked - MPI-531 gates authoring a Flow's app-side UI, not authoring a ComfyUI graph, so this can proceed in parallel. The corrected analysis it starts from is in MPI-4's brief: lipdub is a fourth front end, not a third mask polarity, and everything it needs is already installed.

Implementation started. Bench authoring of the LTX 2.3 lipdub graph: the bench template is read (36 nodes / 49 links), every node type and the ic-lora-lipdub-0.9 LoRA are present on both 8188 and 48188, and plan.md is now written with five phases. It carries one correction to the brief: the audio latent is EMPTY (LTXVEmptyLatentAudio feeds LTXVConcatAVLatent), so the words come from the prompt text and the source audio enters only as speaker-identity ref tokens - swapping that socket swaps the VOICE, not the content. The unused frozen_audio output (noise_mask=0) is the one-link swap that makes the graph audio-driven, so both modes live in one file.
Derived 5 items from the five plan.md phase titles.

Four runs on bench 8188, all status success with 0 node_errors, and NOT ONE moved the mouth. Phase 1 passed cleanly (repo copy byte-identical to the bench, 31 API nodes, 0 missing required / 0 dangling), but two loader substitutions are mandatory - the template names a bf16 transformer and a heretic-fp8 Gemma that do not exist here, so it has never run on this install as written. Drift, the risk the card was written around, did not materialise: 36.1 dB PSNR against the source, identity and lighting intact. The IC-LoRA is applying (37.5 dB between strength 1.0 and 0.0) but its effect is diffuse over the whole subject rather than localised at the mouth. Lightricks README settles what the feature is: text-driven dubbing/rephrasing, where supplied audio is a VOICE reference and frozen_audio is a stage-2 device for the upscale pass - so run 2 misused it, and both this brief and MPI-4 describe the audio front end wrongly. Source framing is ruled out (run 4 gave a head-and-shoulders face at native 960x544). Two suspects remain: the checkpoint (the LoRA is published against ltx-2.3-22b-dev, absent from this machine; we run an int8_convrot distilled-1.1) and the missing stage 2.

IT WORKS, and the variable was face size. Six runs on bench 8188, all status success with 0 node_errors. Runs 1-3 fed a 1920x1088 clip that ResizeImageMaskNode squeezed to 960x544, leaving the head small, and nothing moved. Run 4 fed a head-and-shoulders crop already at 960x544 - same graph, same weights, same seed - and the lips moved with a voice cloned from the supplied reference, confirmed by Fabio watching it. An earlier note here called run 4 motionless; that was a sampling error from twelve late frames while the subject is in profile, and it is corrected in place. Runs 4 and 6 are one link apart and settle the mechanism: with the empty audio latent the model GENERATES the speech from the prompt text and the lips follow it, while with frozen_audio the supplied track is preserved and the lips do not move at all - so the lips follow the audio the model makes, and true audio-preserving lipsync is not available from this IC-LoRA. Supply-an-audio-file therefore needs a speech-to-text step in front, and no Whisper node is installed. Also ported Lightricks official two-stage workflow onto our weights entirely in API format (11 links rewired, dev checkpoint and distilled LoRA replaced by UNETLoader/DualCLIPLoader/VAELoader/VAELoaderKJ) and RAN it: 283s, 1920x1088, clean.
